note: GENERATED by scripts/generate-part-two.mjs from the core lesson — do not hand-edit.
contentObjective: I can draw polygons from their vertex coordinates on the coordinate plane, and use coordinates to find side lengths and solve perimeter and area problems.
languageObjective: I can explain how I found a distance using the words vertices, coordinates, and absolute value.

vocabulary.definition: A corner point of a polygon, named by an ordered pair on the coordinate plane.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un punto de esquina de un polígono, nombrado por un par ordenado en el plano de coordenadas.
vocabulary.visual: The park's corner at (2, 4) — one corner, named by an ordered pair.
vocabulary.cloze: A corner point of a polygon, named by an ordered pair, is a ___.

examples.text: (5, 4), where two sides of the park meet
examples.why: It is a corner, and a coordinate pair names it.
That is a side; a vertex is the point where sides meet.

vocabulary.definition: A closed figure made of line segments; on the plane you draw it by plotting the vertices and connecting them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura cerrada hecha de segmentos; en el plano se dibuja marcando los vértices y conectándolos en orden.
vocabulary.example: Plot the four points, connect them, and the rectangle appears.
vocabulary.visual: Plot (2, 4), (5, 4), (5, −4), (2, −4) and join them — a rectangle appears.
vocabulary.cloze: A closed figure made of line segments is a ___.

examples.text: Four plotted vertices joined in order into a closed rectangle
examples.why: Straight sides, and the figure closes.

examples.text: Three points joined but left open
examples.why: An unclosed path is not a polygon.

vocabulary.definition: The total distance around a polygon — the sum of all its side lengths.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia total alrededor de un polígono: la suma de todos sus lados.
vocabulary.cloze: The total distance around a polygon is its ___.

examples.text: Adding all four side lengths of the rectangle
examples.why: It measures the whole way around.
That gives area — the space inside, not the distance around.

vocabulary.definition: When two vertices share an x- or y-coordinate, the distance between them is the absolute difference of the other coordinates.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuando dos vértices comparten una coordenada x o y, la distancia es la diferencia absoluta de las otras coordenadas.
vocabulary.visual: (2, 4) and (5, 4) share y, so the side is |5 − 2| = 3 units.
vocabulary.cloze: When two vertices share a coordinate, subtract the other and take the ___ ___.

examples.text: |4 − (−4)| = 8 for two vertices that share an x-value
examples.why: Same x means a vertical side, found by subtracting the y-values.
Losing the negative sign collapses the side to nothing.

vocabulary.definition: What one grid unit stands for in the real situation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Lo que representa una unidad de la cuadrícula en la situación real.
vocabulary.example: Each unit is 100 feet, so 3 units of width is 300 feet.
vocabulary.visual: Each grid unit = 100 feet, so 8 units of map is 800 real feet.
vocabulary.cloze: What one grid unit stands for in the real situation is the ___.

examples.text: 1 unit = 100 feet on the park map
examples.why: It converts grid units into real distance.

examples.text: The number of units between two vertices
examples.why: That is a length on the grid; the scale is what a unit means.

vocabulary.definition: The distance between two vertices that are joined by a side.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia entre dos vértices unidos por un lado.
vocabulary.visual: Found with absolute value when the points share a coordinate.
vocabulary.cloze: The distance between two joined vertices is a ___.

examples.why: |−4.25| + |3.5| = 7.75 is the distance along the side.
A coordinate is a position, not a distance.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Maria's Craft Store
revealWordProblem.text:
Maria, a craft store owner, plans to rent a location in a shopping center and is considering the two spaces shown on the grid. Each unit represents one foot, so each line on the grid represents 5 feet. Space A rents for $13.89 per square foot each month, and Space B rents for $13.49 per square foot each month. Maria wants to pay the lower total monthly rent.
Question: Which location would you recommend she rent?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Two shop spaces drawn as polygons on a coordinate grid, labeled Space A and Space B, with vertices at 0 comma 0, 5 comma 35, 15 comma 35, 15 comma 0, and 39 comma 0.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Space A is a trapezoid with parallel horizontal bases 15 feet and 15 − 5 = 10 feet, and height 35 feet. Its area is ½ × (15 + 10) × 35 = 437.5 square feet. Space B is a triangle with base 39 − 15 = 24 feet and height 35 feet, so its area is ½ × 24 × 35 = 420 square feet. Space A costs 437.5 × $13.89 = $6,076.875, or $6,076.88 per month to the nearest cent. Space B costs 420 × $13.49 = $5,665.80 per month. Recommend Space B for the lower total monthly rent. It saves about $411.08 per month while providing 17.5 fewer square feet.

questions.stem: Vertices (-4.5, 3) and (5, 3) share y = 3. What is the distance between them?
questions.explanation: They differ only in x: |5 − (−4.5)| = 5 + 4.5 = 9.5 units.
choiceFeedback: That subtracts 4.5 − 4 or similar — remember the point is at NEGATIVE 4.5, so the distance crosses zero.
That subtracts 5 − 3.5 or mixes an x with a y — use the two x-coordinates only.
hints: Which coordinate is the same? Which differs?
The x-values are −4.5 and 5.
Distance crosses zero: 4.5 to reach 0, then 5 more.
questions.stemEs: Los vértices (-4.5, 3) y (5, 3) comparten y = 3. ¿Cuál es la distancia entre ellos?
questions.explanationEs: Solo se diferencian en x: |5 − (−4.5)| = 5 + 4.5 = 9.5 unidades.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál coordenada es igual? ¿Cuál es distinta?
Los valores de x son −4.5 y 5.
La distancia cruza el cero: 4.5 para llegar a 0, luego 5 más.

questions.stem: Vertices (5, 3) and (5, -3.75) share x = 5. What is the distance between them?
questions.explanation: They differ only in y: |3 − (−3.75)| = 3 + 3.75 = 6.75 units.
choiceFeedback: That subtracts 3.75 − 3 as if both were on the same side of zero.
5 is the shared x-coordinate, not a distance.
That adds 5 + 3.75, mixing the shared x into the answer.
hints: Which coordinate differs?
The y-values are 3 and −3.75.
3 above zero plus 3.75 below zero.
questions.stemEs: Los vértices (5, 3) y (5, -3.75) comparten x = 5. ¿Cuál es la distancia entre ellos?
questions.explanationEs: Solo se diferencian en y: |3 − (−3.75)| = 3 + 3.75 = 6.75 unidades.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál coordenada es distinta?
Los valores de y son 3 y −3.75.
3 arriba del cero más 3.75 abajo del cero.

questions.stem: What is the perimeter of the rectangle with side lengths 9.5 and 6.75 units?
choiceFeedback: 16.25 is 9.5 + 6.75 — that walks only two of the four sides.
64.125 is 9.5 × 6.75 — that is the area, not the perimeter.
hints: A rectangle has four sides.
Each length appears twice.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el perímetro del rectángulo con lados de 9.5 y 6.75 unidades?
hintsEs: Un rectángulo tiene cuatro lados.
Cada longitud aparece dos veces.

steps: 1. Plot all given vertices and connect them in order to form the polygon
2. Find side lengths by counting grid units or using coordinate distance formulas
3. Perimeter = Sum of all side lengths; Area = Use standard polygon formulas
reviewHighlights.watchOut: Subtracting coordinates without the absolute value — from y = 3 down to y = −3.75 the distance is 3 + 3.75 = 6.75 units, not 3.75 − 3 = 0.75. Distances that cross zero are the whole reason the absolute value is there.

level1.stem: Find the length of the side from (−3, 5) to (4, 5).
level1.stemEs: Halla la longitud del lado de (−3, 5) a (4, 5).
hints: Both points have y = 5. Add the distances from 0.
hintsEs: Los dos puntos tienen y = 5. Suma las distancias desde 0.
level1.explanation: Find the coordinate that is the same: y = 5 Add the distances from 0: 3 + 4 = 7
level1.explanationEs: Halla la coordenada que es igual: y = 5 Suma las distancias desde 0: 3 + 4 = 7

level1.stem: A rectangle has vertices (−2, 1), (3, 1), (3, −3) and (−2, −3). Find its perimeter.
level1.stemEs: Un rectángulo tiene vértices (−2, 1), (3, 1), (3, −3) y (−2, −3). Halla su perímetro.
hints: Find one side across and one side up and down. Then add all four sides.
hintsEs: Halla un lado de lado a lado y uno de arriba abajo. Luego suma los cuatro lados.
level1.explanation: Find the two side lengths: 2 + 3 = 5; 1 + 3 = 4 Add all four sides: 5 + 4 + 5 + 4 = 18
level1.explanationEs: Halla las dos longitudes: 2 + 3 = 5; 1 + 3 = 4 Suma los cuatro lados: 5 + 4 + 5 + 4 = 18

level1.stem: A rectangle has vertices (−2, 5), (4, 5), (4, 2) and (−2, 2). Find its area.
level1.stemEs: Un rectángulo tiene vértices (−2, 5), (4, 5), (4, 2) y (−2, 2). Halla su área.
hints: Find the length and the width. Then multiply.
hintsEs: Halla el largo y el ancho. Luego multiplica.
level1.explanation: Find the two side lengths: 2 + 4 = 6; 5 − 2 = 3 Multiply for the area: 6 × 3 = 18
level1.explanationEs: Halla las dos longitudes: 2 + 4 = 6; 5 − 2 = 3 Multiplica para hallar el área: 6 × 3 = 18

level1.stem: A rectangle has vertices (1, 2), (7, 2), (7, 5) and (1, 5). Find its perimeter.
level1.stemEs: Un rectángulo tiene vértices (1, 2), (7, 2), (7, 5) y (1, 5). Halla su perímetro.
hints: Find one side across and one side up and down. Each length appears two times.
hintsEs: Halla un lado de lado a lado y uno de arriba abajo. Cada longitud aparece dos veces.
level1.explanation: Find the two side lengths: 7 − 1 = 6; 5 − 2 = 3 Add all four sides: 2 × 6 + 2 × 3 = 12 + 6 = 18
level1.explanationEs: Halla las dos longitudes: 7 − 1 = 6; 5 − 2 = 3 Suma los cuatro lados: 2 × 6 + 2 × 3 = 12 + 6 = 18

level1.stem: A rectangle has vertices (−1.5, 3), (4, 3), (4, −2) and (−1.5, −2). Find its perimeter.
level1.stemEs: Un rectángulo tiene vértices (−1.5, 3), (4, 3), (4, −2) y (−1.5, −2). Halla su perímetro.
hints: Each side crosses an axis. Add the distances from 0.
hintsEs: Cada lado cruza un eje. Suma las distancias desde 0.
level1.explanation: Find the side across: 1.5 + 4 = 5.5 Find the side up and down: 3 + 2 = 5 Add all four sides: 2 × 5.5 + 2 × 5 = 11 + 10 = 21
level1.explanationEs: Halla el lado de lado a lado: 1.5 + 4 = 5.5 Halla el lado de arriba abajo: 3 + 2 = 5 Suma los cuatro lados: 2 × 5.5 + 2 × 5 = 11 + 10 = 21

level2.stem: Sam says the rectangle with vertices (−5, 1), (3, 1), (3, 4) and (−5, 4) has a perimeter of 8 + 3 = 11 units. Is he right? What is the perimeter?
level2.stemEs: Sam dice que el rectángulo con vértices (−5, 1), (3, 1), (3, 4) y (−5, 4) tiene un perímetro de 8 + 3 = 11 unidades. ¿Tiene razón? ¿Cuál es el perímetro?
hints: A rectangle has four sides. How many sides did Sam add?
hintsEs: Un rectángulo tiene cuatro lados. ¿Cuántos lados sumó Sam?
level2.explanation: Find the two side lengths: 5 + 3 = 8; 4 − 1 = 3 Add all four sides: 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22
level2.explanationEs: Halla las dos longitudes: 5 + 3 = 8; 4 − 1 = 3 Suma los cuatro lados: 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22

level2.stem: A rectangle has vertices (−6, 2), (−1, 2) and (−1, −3). The fourth vertex is (−6, ?). What is the missing y-coordinate?
level2.stemEs: Un rectángulo tiene vértices (−6, 2), (−1, 2) y (−1, −3). El cuarto vértice es (−6, ?). ¿Cuál es la coordenada y que falta?
hints: The fourth vertex is on the same horizontal line as (−1, −3).
hintsEs: El cuarto vértice está en la misma línea horizontal que (−1, −3).
level2.explanation: Match the x of (−6, 2): x = −6 Match the y of (−1, −3): y = −3
level2.explanationEs: Usa la misma x que (−6, 2): x = −6 Usa la misma y que (−1, −3): y = −3

level2.stem: A rectangle has vertices (−3, 6), (3, 6), (3, 2) and (−3, 2). Find its perimeter.
level2.stemEs: Un rectángulo tiene vértices (−3, 6), (3, 6), (3, 2) y (−3, 2). Halla su perímetro.
hints: Find the side across and the side up and down. Then add all four sides.
hintsEs: Halla el lado de lado a lado y el de arriba abajo. Luego suma los cuatro lados.
level2.explanation: Find the two side lengths: 3 + 3 = 6; 6 − 2 = 4 Add all four sides: 2 × 6 + 2 × 4 = 12 + 8 = 20
level2.explanationEs: Halla las dos longitudes: 3 + 3 = 6; 6 − 2 = 4 Suma los cuatro lados: 2 × 6 + 2 × 4 = 12 + 8 = 20

level2.stem: The top side of a rectangle goes from (−3, 4) to (5, 4). The area is 48 square units. What is the y-coordinate of the bottom side?
level2.stemEs: El lado de arriba de un rectángulo va de (−3, 4) a (5, 4). El área es 48 unidades cuadradas. ¿Cuál es la coordenada y del lado de abajo?
hints: Find the length of the top side. Then use the area to find the height.
hintsEs: Halla la longitud del lado de arriba. Luego usa el área para hallar la altura.
level2.explanation: Find the top side: 3 + 5 = 8 Divide the area by 8: 48 ÷ 8 = 6 Move down 6 from y = 4: 4 − 6 = −2
level2.explanationEs: Halla el lado de arriba: 3 + 5 = 8 Divide el área entre 8: 48 ÷ 8 = 6 Baja 6 desde y = 4: 4 − 6 = −2

level2.stem: A soccer field on a map has corners (−50, 30), (50, 30), (50, −30) and (−50, −30). Each unit is 1 yard. How many yards is it around the field?
level2.stemEs: Una cancha de fútbol en un mapa tiene esquinas (−50, 30), (50, 30), (50, −30) y (−50, −30). Cada unidad es 1 yarda. ¿Cuántas yardas mide el contorno de la cancha?
hints: "Around the field" means perimeter. Each side crosses an axis.
hintsEs: "El contorno de la cancha" quiere decir el perímetro. Cada lado cruza un eje.
level2.explanation: Find the two side lengths: 50 + 50 = 100; 30 + 30 = 60 Add all four sides: 2 × 100 + 2 × 60 = 200 + 120 = 320
level2.explanationEs: Halla las dos longitudes: 50 + 50 = 100; 30 + 30 = 60 Suma los cuatro lados: 2 × 100 + 2 × 60 = 200 + 120 = 320

level3.stem: A rectangle has vertices at (1, 1), (7, 1), (7, 5), and (1, 5). What is its perimeter?
choiceFeedback: That adds one of each side. Each length appears twice around a rectangle.
That doubles the horizontal side only. The two vertical sides of 4 units each still count.
That is the AREA, 6 times 4, in square units. Perimeter adds the four side lengths.
level3.explanation: The horizontal sides are |7 − 1| = 6 units and the vertical sides are |5 − 1| = 4 units. Perimeter = 2(6) + 2(4) = 20 units.

level3.stem: Space A has corners (0, 0), (20, 0), (20, 20) and (0, 20). Space B has corners (0, 0), (30, 0), (30, 12) and (0, 12). Each unit is 1 foot. Which space has more floor area?
level3.stemEs: El espacio A tiene esquinas (0, 0), (20, 0), (20, 20) y (0, 20). El espacio B tiene esquinas (0, 0), (30, 0), (30, 12) y (0, 12). Cada unidad es 1 pie. ¿Qué espacio tiene más área de piso?
hints: Find the length and width of each space. Then find each area.
hintsEs: Halla el largo y el ancho de cada espacio. Luego halla cada área.
level3.explanation: Find the area of Space A: 20 × 20 = 400 Find the area of Space B: 30 × 12 = 360 Compare the areas: 400 > 360
level3.explanationEs: Halla el área del espacio A: 20 × 20 = 400 Halla el área del espacio B: 30 × 12 = 360 Compara las áreas: 400 > 360
choiceFeedback: Space B has a longer side, but its area is 30 × 12 = 360. That is less than 20 × 20 = 400.
Find each area: 20 × 20 = 400 and 30 × 12 = 360. They are not equal.

level3.stem: Three vertices of a rectangle are (−4, 2), (4, 2) and (4, −3). What is the area of the rectangle?
level3.stemEs: Tres vértices de un rectángulo son (−4, 2), (4, 2) y (4, −3). ¿Cuál es el área del rectángulo?
hints: You do not need the fourth vertex to find the two side lengths.
hintsEs: No necesitas el cuarto vértice para hallar las dos longitudes.
level3.explanation: Find the side across: 4 + 4 = 8 Find the side up and down: 2 + 3 = 5 Multiply for the area: 8 × 5 = 40
level3.explanationEs: Halla el lado de lado a lado: 4 + 4 = 8 Halla el lado de arriba abajo: 2 + 3 = 5 Multiplica para hallar el área: 8 × 5 = 40

level3.stem: A school draws its playground on a grid. The corners are (−20, 10), (25, 10), (25, −10) and (−20, −10). Each unit is 1 meter. How many meters of fence go all the way around?
level3.stemEs: Una escuela dibuja su patio en una cuadrícula. Las esquinas son (−20, 10), (25, 10), (25, −10) y (−20, −10). Cada unidad es 1 metro. ¿Cuántos metros de cerca rodean todo el patio?
hints: A fence all the way around is the perimeter. Each side crosses an axis.
hintsEs: Una cerca alrededor de todo es el perímetro. Cada lado cruza un eje.
level3.explanation: Find the two side lengths: 20 + 25 = 45; 10 + 10 = 20 Add all four sides: 2 × 45 + 2 × 20 = 90 + 40 = 130
level3.explanationEs: Halla las dos longitudes: 20 + 25 = 45; 10 + 10 = 20 Suma los cuatro lados: 2 × 45 + 2 × 20 = 90 + 40 = 130

level3.stem: A polygon has vertices (−4, 3), (2, 3), (2, 0), (5, 0), (5, −2) and (−4, −2). Find its area.
level3.stemEs: Un polígono tiene vértices (−4, 3), (2, 3), (2, 0), (5, 0), (5, −2) y (−4, −2). Halla su área.
hints: Cut the shape along the x-axis. Find the area of each rectangle.
hintsEs: Corta la figura por el eje x. Halla el área de cada rectángulo.
level3.explanation: Find the top rectangle: 6 × 3 = 18 Find the bottom rectangle: 9 × 2 = 18 Add the two areas: 18 + 18 = 36
level3.explanationEs: Halla el rectángulo de arriba: 6 × 3 = 18 Halla el rectángulo de abajo: 9 × 2 = 18 Suma las dos áreas: 18 + 18 = 36

tool.title: Perimeter of the Rectangle (−3, 2), (4, 2), (4, −1), (−3, −1)
tool.caption: The two horizontal sides are each |4 − (−3)| = 7 units and the two vertical sides are each |2 − (−1)| = 3 units, so the perimeter is 7 + 7 + 3 + 3 = 20 units.

steps.title: Find Space A's area (trapezoid)
steps.say: Space A has two parallel bases, so use the trapezoid formula.

steps.title: Find each monthly rent
steps.say: Multiply each area by its price per square foot.

steps.title: Compare the rents
steps.say: Space B is a little smaller but costs less each month.

workedSteps.answer: Recommend Space B: $5,665.80 a month, about $411.08 less than Space A ($6,076.88), with 17.5 fewer square feet.
